tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). # JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

## 2.0 Project-window hierarchy

The Project window should not treat Prepare, Preview, and Info as three equal destinations.

- **Prepare is the dominant, persistent workspace.** It is where users inspect the model, communicate intent, manipulate geometry, resolve uncertainty, and review the agent's plan.
- **Check print opens Orca Preview in a modal window.** Prepare remains underneath; closing Check returns focus to Prepare. It is a secondary action when the active plate has a valid slice.
- **Info becomes Project details.** It is a drawer opened from the project name or menu. The agent reads its contents continuously even when the drawer is closed.
- **Print opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog.** It never sends directly. The person's Send in that dialog remains the consequential commitment.

The normal flow is:

`Prepare -> Check print -> return to Prepare if correction is needed -> Print -> OrcaSlicer's send dialog -> the person presses Send`

### Default Project-window composition

The default window should contain:

- Project name and saved/unsaved state
- Compact printer pointer: target printer, nozzle, build plate, and material
- Compact, editable intent summary
- Compact active plate/object summary
- 3D Prepare canvas
- Essential direct-manipulation tools
- Compact pinned agent plan
- Highest unresolved assumption, compromise, or risk
- Check print
- Print
- Consequential warnings when applicable

The canvas is the primary human-agent collaboration surface. It must make the build plate and model visible, support camera rotation, pan, zoom, selection, and direct spatial manipulation, and show the changes the agent makes.

The compact summaries should keep the governing assumptions visible without expanding full editors. Examples:

> Decorative · appearance first · protect front surface · under 5 hours

> Plate 1 · Fuzzy Heart · 1 copy · PLA Matte

A one-object project should not permanently display a large object tree. A complete intent questionnaire should not remain expanded after it has been answered.

In the Agent pane the intent summary and the pinned plan are the top of the setup card: the purpose in the person's words and the plan's headline in the agent's, each shown only once written, above the presets and estimates in force. The card warns only about a line it shows, as an annotation of that line, such as a plan the project has moved on from; other risks stay with the canvas, the chat and the printer chip (see the setup card in [Design System](design-system.md#components-and-states)).

### Direct resolution of uncertainty

Warnings should link to the user action that resolves them rather than expecting the user to translate them into legacy slicer controls:

- `Support enters this hole` -> `Protect this opening`
- `Seam crosses a visible face` -> `Mark visible face`
- `Strength direction is unclear` -> `Show load direction`
- `Part may not fit` -> `Enter critical dimension`
- `Support may be hard to remove` -> `Adjust supports`

Each feature still has one authoritative home, but summaries, warnings, and resolution actions may appear elsewhere. For example, Printer Configuration owns the installed hardware state while Prepare shows a compact pointer and any mismatch.

## 2.1 Project knowledge

This surface answers: **What is this project, and what does someone need to know about it?**

OrcaSlicer exposes model descriptions, creator information, pictures, license information, profile notes, accessories, bills of materials, assembly guides, and other attachments.

A project inspected during product discovery contained a safety instruction limiting it to electric tea lights. That information could affect how the agent evaluates material, temperature exposure, and intended use.

### Why the agent cannot decide this alone

The mesh does not contain reliable authorship, licensing, safety, assembly, or use-case information. An agent may extract clues, but it must not treat guesses as project facts.

content.content:
Home is the hub for:

- Printer cards showing availability, condition, and loaded filament
- Project gallery, open, and project status
- Opening 3MF, STL, STEP, SVG, OBJ, AMF, and ZIP files, each as a new project (Open… and the page as a drop target; see [Opening and importing files](architecture.md#opening-and-importing-files))
- Entry to project versions and backups
- Launching Monitor

## 3.2 Project window

The Project window contains the print-planning lifecycle without dividing it into equal destinations:

- **Prepare:** dominant workspace containing intent, objects and plates, the 3D canvas, geometry editing, local meaning, and the agent plan
- **Check print:** temporary sliced-verification mode
- **Project details:** drawer for authoritative project knowledge
- **Print:** opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog

Prepare may point to Printer Configuration, but it does not own machine calibration, filament inventory, maintenance, or privacy settings.

## 3.3 Printer Configuration

Printer Configuration owns:

- Target printer, nozzle, and build-plate configuration
- Loaded filament, material colors, AMS, and multi-material inventory
- Calibration workflows
- Troubleshooting and maintenance
- Firmware-update timing
- Camera and monitoring privacy
- Network plugins and diagnostic tools
- Stored printer files and timelapses

Prepare displays a compact pointer to this state and surfaces mismatches; it does not duplicate the complete configuration UI.

## 3.4 Monitor

Monitor is a pop-out surface so it can remain visible while the user works elsewhere. It owns:

- Camera
- Progress, current layer, and remaining time
- Printer state
- Nozzle and bed temperatures
- Health and fault alerts
- Pause, Resume, and Stop as never-hidden human overrides

Manual movement, homing, detailed fan or light control, storage, and file management are contextual.

## 3.5 Overlays and application-level layers

- **Send dialog:** OrcaSlicer's own send dialog in JusPrin colours: destination, plate, material mapping and send options, then the person's Send
- **Expert layer:** raw process settings, numeric per-object and per-region overrides, manual calibration ranges, toolpath diagnostics, and G-code
- **Preferences:** cloud region, stealth/offline behavior, network plugins, sync, updates, privacy, backup and recovery, import/export administration, and developer tools

This structure preserves the lifecycle of a print without turning Setup, Intent, Plan, Verify, Print, Monitor, and Diagnose into nine equal screens.

---

# 4. Visibility hierarchy

## 4.1 Default

Continuously visible in the ordinary Project window:

- Project name and saved/unsaved state
- Current printer, nozzle, plate, and material summary
- Compact intent summary
- Compact active plate and object summary
- 3D Prepare canvas
- Add, remove, select, move, rotate, scale, place on face, arrange, duplicate, Undo, and Redo
- Compact agent plan
- Highest unresolved assumption or risk
- Check print and Print

Inside Check, the default changes to sliced appearance, time, material, cost, the highest-priority warning, and comparison with intent. When supports exist, support placement and removal risk become the default Check emphasis.

## 4.2 Contextual

Shown when the project or current task makes it relevant:

- Full object, part, and plate tree
- Per-object material or extruder
- Modifiers, support enforcers, blockers, print order, and search
- Local surface annotations and object-specific requirements
- Mirror, cut, split, merge, assemble, text, measure, repair, positive/negative parts, and multi-plate distribution
- Seam, bridge, overhang, thin-feature, first-layer, island, and collision inspection
- Material changes, purge waste, prime tower, and extruder assignments
- Time and material estimate in Prepare after a valid background slice exists
- Assembly instructions, accessories, and reference pictures
- Calibration and maintenance recommendations
- Firmware updates, storage, timelapses, and multi-device management

## 4.3 On demand

Available through Project details, More, or the expert layer:

- Full intent questionnaire after it has been completed
- Project description, author, license, pictures, BOM, assembly guide, and profile notes
- Version, backup, ownership, and export administration
- Detailed agent rationale, alternatives, confidence, profile deviations, and change history
- Individual speeds and accelerations
-----ARCH-----
- not depend on `GUI_ObjectList` for commands that change the model;
- offer plate selection, object import and addition, and the other commands the product needs;
- keep wxWidgets types and OrcaSlicer types out of its public interface.

Sometimes the operation you need exists only inside OrcaSlicer's UI code. In that case, add the smallest possible command to the OrcaSlicer class that already does the work, and name it for what it does. Do not copy the operation into JusPrin. Do not fake clicks or key presses on hidden controls.

### Canvas presentation

`GLCanvas3D` keeps a small API for controlling how its parts are presented. That API contains nothing specific to JusPrin. A controller in fork-owned code uses the API to apply JusPrin's choices, and puts OrcaSlicer's previous state back when the controller is destroyed. Whether a control is drawn and whether it receives input must be two separate switches. Otherwise a control that is hidden could still swallow pointer events. OrcaSlicer's native gizmos (the on-canvas tools such as Move and Rotate) must stay usable while one is active.

The Check print window's preview has its own controller, `PreviewPresentationController` beside `CanvasPresentationController`. It hides the canvas's legacy overlay layer (plate selector strip, 3D navigator, canvas toolbar), holds OrcaSlicer's app-wide G-code listing preference (`show_gcode_window`) off while the window is open, and switches the legend through `GCodeViewer::show_legend`; destroying it restores all three, on every close path. Both sliders stay as OrcaSlicer draws them. OrcaSlicer's single ImGui context also keeps the last pointer position of whichever canvas saw it, so the window clears it when it opens and when the pointer leaves its canvas.

The POC had one broad switch, `render_overlays`. Production needs finer control. Treat each of these as its own item that can be shown or hidden separately: OrcaSlicer's main toolbar, the gizmo picker, the handles of the active gizmo, plate actions, object labels, layer-editing controls, navigation aids, the Preview legend, and the Preview sliders. Some controls are shared between canvases, such as `Plater`'s collapse toolbar. A shared control must be saved and restored by one object that lives as long as the shell does. Do not give each canvas its own guard for it.

### Plates and Project pane

This pane is native code owned by the fork (`Shell/LeftPane`). It sits to the left of the workspace on Prepare. Its first tab lists every plate, even when the project has only one. Its second tab shows the saved project's identity, the model's 3MF metadata, the history of physical prints, the version history, and export. The pane keeps no project state of its own and has no undo of its own. It draws what two model classes describe, and those classes do not depend on the GUI. Every click calls a workspace command.

| Piece | What it is responsible for |
|---|---|
| `Workspace/ProjectOutline.hpp`, `IWorkspace::outline()` | The data the pane reads: plates, copies of objects (each with the plate that holds it), volumes, facts about customization and the mesh, and what is selected below the object level. Which plate a copy is on comes from `PartPlateList`. The code never guesses it from where the copy sits. |
| `Shell/LeftPaneModel` | Which rows the Plates tab shows, and when. The active plate is open. Other plates are folded, each with a summary computed from its current copies. A row has child rows only when there is data for them. "Not on a plate" appears only when some copy is on no plate. This class also handles switching between the tabs and between the views inside the Project tab. |
| `Shell/ProjectPaneModel` | The contents of the Details and Print history views, as plain data. A field that nobody filled in is left out. The slicer's time estimate and the measured print duration are kept as separate values. A ledger record that has nothing to display is included in the count but gets no row. |
| `Workspace/OrcaOutline.cpp` | The commands, implemented on top of OrcaSlicer: `select_plate`, `add_plate`, `select_copy`, `select_volume`, `plate_actions`, `run_plate_action`. Each command ends by calling the same code OrcaSlicer's own UI calls (`Plater::select_plate_by_hover_id`, the toolbar's Add plate event, `Selection` plus the canvas's object-select event). The events are raised synchronously on the GUI thread, so the change has already happened when the command returns. |
| `Shell/LeftPane`, `LeftPaneProject.cpp` | Drawing and input. While drawing, the pane records where each control ended up. Pointer handling looks each click up in that record, so a click can only hit something that was actually drawn. |

The ledger is the record of physical prints. It can have any number of subscribers, through `ProjectPersistence::subscribe_ledger`. The pane and the header's overflow menu each subscribe to it separately.

### Opening and importing files

Decided 2026-10-24. A file reaches JusPrin in a handful of ways, and they mean one of two things: **start from this file**, or **add this to the project I am working on**. The first is what a person means almost every time they bring a file in; the second is the minority case (a multi-part print), and the person signals it by aiming at the plate or by asking the agent. Because autosave keeps every project, starting a new project by mistake costs one click on Recent, while adding to the wrong project leaves a stray part in it. So every way in starts a new project unless the person aimed at the plate.

| How the file is opened | Model file (STL, STEP, OBJ, AMF, …) | .3mf |
|---|---|---|
| Opened from the OS: a double-click in Finder or Explorer, "Open with", a browser's "open in JusPrin" | New project, named after the file; the app goes to Prepare | New project; the "Previously opened file" question if the file was opened before |
| Dropped on Home | Same | Same |
| Home's **Open…** button, File › Open Project (Cmd+O) | Same | Same |
| Dropped on the Prepare canvas | Added to the open project | New project, as above. OrcaSlicer's "open as project or import geometry?" question is not asked |
| **+ Add model** in the Plates and Project pane, File › Import (Cmd+I) | Added to the open project | Its geometry is added to the open project, without its settings (OrcaSlicer's Import) |
| The Agent composer's + › 3D model, a drop on the Agent pane, or a request in the chat | Attached; the agent adds it to the open project (`object_import`) | Same |

Rules that follow from the table:

- A model file never silently lands in whatever project happened to be open behind Home. Before 2026-10-24 Home's Import button did exactly that, because it called OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, and from 2026-09-30 a project was always open behind Home (the most recent one resumes at startup).
- A file opened from the OS lands in the running JusPrin. OrcaSlicer's default starts a second process for a .3mf; JusPrin runs as a single instance on every platform.
- Several files opened or dropped together make one new project holding all of them.

Continuously visible in the ordinary Project window:

- Project name and saved/unsaved state
- Current printer, nozzle, plate, and material summary
- Compact intent summary
- Compact active plate and object summary
- 3D Prepare canvas
- Add, remove, select, move, rotate, scale, place on face, arrange, duplicate, Undo, and Redo
- Compact agent plan
- Highest unresolved assumption or risk
- Check print and Print

Inside Check, the default changes to sliced appearance, time, material, cost, the highest-priority warning, and comparison with intent. When supports exist, support placement and removal risk become the default Check emphasis.

## 4.2 Contextual

Shown when the project or current task makes it relevant:

- Full object, part, and plate tree
- Per-object material or extruder
- Modifiers, support enforcers, blockers, print order, and search
- Local surface annotations and object-specific requirements
- Mirror, cut, split, merge, assemble, text, measure, repair, positive/negative parts, and multi-plate distribution
- Seam, bridge, overhang, thin-feature, first-layer, island, and collision inspection
- Material changes, purge waste, prime tower, and extruder assignments
- Time and material estimate in Prepare after a valid background slice exists
- Assembly instructions, accessories, and reference pictures
- Calibration and maintenance recommendations
- Firmware updates, storage, timelapses, and multi-device management

## 4.3 On demand

Available through Project details, More, or the expert layer:

- Full intent questionnaire after it has been completed
- Project description, author, license, pictures, BOM, assembly guide, and profile notes
- Version, backup, ownership, and export administration
- Detailed agent rationale, alternatives, confidence, profile deviations, and change history
- Individual speeds and accelerations
-----ARCH-----
- not depend on `GUI_ObjectList` for commands that change the model;
- offer plate selection, object import and addition, and the other commands the product needs;

### Canvas presentation

`GLCanvas3D` keeps a small API for controlling how its parts are presented. That API contains nothing specific to JusPrin. A controller in fork-owned code uses the API to apply JusPrin's choices, and puts OrcaSlicer's previous state back when the controller is destroyed. Whether a control is drawn and whether it receives input must be two separate switches. Otherwise a control that is hidden could still swallow pointer events. OrcaSlicer's native gizmos (the on-canvas tools such as Move and Rotate) must stay usable while one is active.

The Check print window's preview has its own controller, `PreviewPresentationController` beside `CanvasPresentationController`. It hides the canvas's legacy overlay layer (plate selector strip, 3D navigator, canvas toolbar), holds OrcaSlicer's app-wide G-code listing preference (`show_gcode_window`) off while the window is open, and switches the legend through `GCodeViewer::show_legend`; destroying it restores all three, on every close path. Both sliders stay as OrcaSlicer draws them. OrcaSlicer's single ImGui context also keeps the last pointer position of whichever canvas saw it, so the window clears it when it opens and when the pointer leaves its canvas.

The POC had one broad switch, `render_overlays`. Production needs finer control. Treat each of these as its own item that can be shown or hidden separately: OrcaSlicer's main toolbar, the gizmo picker, the handles of the active gizmo, plate actions, object labels, layer-editing controls, navigation aids, the Preview legend, and the Preview sliders. Some controls are shared between canvases, such as `Plater`'s collapse toolbar. A shared control must be saved and restored by one object that lives as long as the shell does. Do not give each canvas its own guard for it.

### Plates and Project pane

This pane is native code owned by the fork (`Shell/LeftPane`). It sits to the left of the workspace on Prepare. Its first tab lists every plate, even when the project has only one. Its second tab shows the saved project's identity, the model's 3MF metadata, the history of physical prints, the version history, and export. The pane keeps no project state of its own and has no undo of its own. It draws what two model classes describe, and those classes do not depend on the GUI. Every click calls a workspace command.

| Piece | What it is responsible for |
|---|---|
| `Workspace/ProjectOutline.hpp`, `IWorkspace::outline()` | The data the pane reads: plates, copies of objects (each with the plate that holds it), volumes, facts about customization and the mesh, and what is selected below the object level. Which plate a copy is on comes from `PartPlateList`. The code never guesses it from where the copy sits. |
| `Shell/LeftPaneModel` | Which rows the Plates tab shows, and when. The active plate is open. Other plates are folded, each with a summary computed from its current copies. A row has child rows only when there is data for them. "Not on a plate" appears only when some copy is on no plate. This class also handles switching between the tabs and between the views inside the Project tab. |
| `Shell/ProjectPaneModel` | The contents of the Details and Print history views, as plain data. A field that nobody filled in is left out. The slicer's time estimate and the measured print duration are kept as separate values. A ledger record that has nothing to display is included in the count but gets no row. |
| `Workspace/OrcaOutline.cpp` | The commands, implemented on top of OrcaSlicer: `select_plate`, `add_plate`, `select_copy`, `select_volume`, `plate_actions`, `run_plate_action`. Each command ends by calling the same code OrcaSlicer's own UI calls (`Plater::select_plate_by_hover_id`, the toolbar's Add plate event, `Selection` plus the canvas's object-select event). The events are raised synchronously on the GUI thread, so the change has already happened when the command returns. |

### Opening and importing files

Decided 2026-10-24. A file reaches JusPrin in a handful of ways, and they mean one of two things: **start from this file**, or **add this to the project I am working on**. The first is what a person means almost every time they bring a file in; the second is the minority case (a multi-part print), and the person signals it by aiming at the plate or by asking the agent. Because autosave keeps every project, starting a new project by mistake costs one click on Recent, while adding to the wrong project leaves a stray part in it. So every way in starts a new project unless the person aimed at the plate.

| Dropped on Home | Same | Same |
| Home's **Open…** button, File › Open Project (Cmd+O) | Same | Same |
| Dropped on the Prepare canvas | Added to the open project | New project, as above. OrcaSlicer's "open as project or import geometry?" question is not asked |

- Project gallery, open, and project status
- Opening 3MF, STL, STEP, SVG, OBJ, AMF, and ZIP files, each as a new project (Open… and the page as a drop target; see [Opening and importing files](architecture.md#opening-and-importing-files))
- Entry to project versions and backups
- Launching Monitor

The Project window contains the print-planning lifecycle without dividing it into equal destinations:

- **Prepare:** dominant workspace containing intent, objects and plates, the 3D canvas, geometry editing, local meaning, and the agent plan
- **Check print:** temporary sliced-verification mode
- **Project details:** drawer for authoritative project knowledge
- **Print:** opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog

Prepare may point to Printer Configuration, but it does not own machine calibration, filament inventory, maintenance, or privacy settings.

## 3.3 Printer Configuration

Printer Configuration owns:

- Target printer, nozzle, and build-plate configuration
- Loaded filament, material colors, AMS, and multi-material inventory
- Calibration workflows
- Troubleshooting and maintenance
- Firmware-update timing
- Camera and monitoring privacy
- Network plugins and diagnostic tools
- Stored printer files and timelapses

Prepare displays a compact pointer to this state and surfaces mismatches; it does not duplicate the complete configuration UI.

## 3.4 Monitor

Monitor is a pop-out surface so it can remain visible while the user works elsewhere. It owns:

- Camera
- Progress, current layer, and remaining time
- Printer state
- Nozzle and bed temperatures
- Health and fault alerts
- Pause, Resume, and Stop as never-hidden human overrides

Manual movement, homing, detailed fan or light control, storage, and file management are contextual.

## 3.5 Overlays and application-level layers

- **Send dialog:** OrcaSlicer's own send dialog in JusPrin colours: destination, plate, material mapping and send options, then the person's Send
- **Expert layer:** raw process settings, numeric per-object and per-region overrides, manual calibration ranges, toolpath diagnostics, and G-code
- **Preferences:** cloud region, stealth/offline behavior, network plugins, sync, updates, privacy, backup and recovery, import/export administration, and developer tools

the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

content.content:
the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

# Prepare header: what the "…" menu holds and what it should hold

Written 2026-10-27 from the code on `jusprin-newui` (StatusRow.cpp, LeftPaneProject.cpp, PrinterMenu.cpp, FilamentMenu.cpp, ShellController.cpp, HomeUI App.tsx) and `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`. Untracked working note; not for commit.

## What the Prepare screen does

Prepare is the project window of the new shell. One header row sits across the top:

- Left: Home, and the toggle for the Plates and Project pane when that pane is closed.
- Centre: the printer-and-filament chip. Its printer half opens a menu (other printers, Printer settings…, Calibrate…, Add a printer…); its filament half opens the slot menu (filaments, colours, Use what's loaded on the printer…, Filament settings…, Calibrate this filament…).
- Right: the split print button (Slice / Print plate N, with Check Print, Print…, Print all plates…, Export sliced file… in its dropdown), the "…" overflow button, and the Agent-panel toggle.

Under the header: the Plates and Project pane on the left (plate rows with Rename, Arrange, Auto-orient, Lock, Plate settings…, Delete; + Add model, + Add plate; a Project tab with the project name and save state, Details, Version history, Export project 3MF…, Print history, Edit Project Info), the 3D canvas with the tool strip (Move, Rotate, Scale, Add instance, More = OrcaSlicer's right-click menu), and the Agent pane (chat, setup card, All settings, chat navigation, Preferences › Agent for setup).

OrcaSlicer's own menus stay on screen on every platform: the macOS menu bar (File, Edit, View, Window, Help) and, on Windows and Linux, OrcaSlicer's title bar with the same dropdowns plus Undo and Redo. The shell removes only the Calibration menu. So every OrcaSlicer command is still reachable, and the overflow menu does not need to carry them.

## The menu today

1. Project name with its save state ("Saved", "Saving…", "Couldn't save", "Unsaved changes"): a title row, not clickable. A warning row is added under it when autosave failed or old project data couldn't be removed.
2. Recent projects… (eight at a time, "Older projects…" pages on; opening one swaps the project in place)
3. Back to Prepare
4. Preferences… (⌘, / Ctrl+,)
5. Switch to classic view… (uninstalls the shell and shows stock OrcaSlicer)

What is wrong with it:

- The project name is a row you cannot click, and when the Plates and Project pane is closed it is the only place on Prepare that shows the name. The product definition says the name and save state are continuously visible, and that Project details opens "from the project name or menu". Neither holds today.
- "Back to Prepare" sits on the Prepare screen. It is there because Tab on the canvas still flips OrcaSlicer to its Preview tab under the JusPrin header (GLCanvas3D posts the tab event; the shell's key hook only handles Ctrl+,). Check print itself is a modal now, so the row is a repair for a leak, shown all the time.
- Four different scopes in one list: this project, navigation, the app, and an escape hatch.

## Proposal

Keep the "…" glyph, not a gear. On Home the gear is a plain button that opens Preferences; on Prepare the menu is mostly actions on this project. A gear that opens a mixed menu here and Preferences there would mean two things. (If the menu is cut down to app-only rows instead, see option B, then a gear is right, and Home's gear should become the same menu.)

### Option A (recommended): this project, then the app

Group 1, this project:

- **Project name · Saved** — clickable: opens the Project tab in the Plates and Project pane (opening the pane if it is closed). The autosave warning rows stay under it as now.
- **Version history** — the Project tab's Versions view.
- **Export project 3MF…** — the same command the Project tab runs.
- **Recent projects ›** — as now. Kept because it is the fast switch; Home is where you browse.

Group 2, the app:

- **Preferences…** ⌘, — as now.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** — optional. OrcaSlicer's dialog lists shortcuts for controls the shell hides, so it needs a JusPrin list or a pass over the dialog first.
- **Report a problem…** — optional, only once there is a destination (support address, GitHub issues, or a log bundle). Nothing in the code does this today.
- **Switch to classic view…** — last, after a separator, as now.

Remove **Back to Prepare** as a standing row. Either show it only while OrcaSlicer's Preview tab is the selected one, or stop the Tab flip at the shell (the real fix) and drop the row.

Deliberately not in the menu, and where each lives: Add model (the pane's + Add model, a drop on the canvas, File › Import); printer and filament settings and calibration (the chip's two menus); process settings (All settings in the Agent pane; OrcaSlicer's process tab is not opened from the shell anywhere today); Check print, Print, Export sliced file (the print button); showing and hiding the panes (the header toggles); new chat and chat history (the Agent pane); version, update check, the projects folder (the Preferences window shows all three); Monitor (Home and the printer).

### Option B: app-only gear, same on both screens

Gear on Home and Prepare opening the same menu: Preferences…, Keyboard shortcuts, Report a problem…, Switch to classic view…. The project rows leave the menu: Version history and Export are in the Project tab, Recent projects goes back to Home. Consequence: with the pane closed, nothing on Prepare shows the project name, so a name label would have to be added to the header itself (between Home and the centred chip, which only fits on wide windows).

### Option C: both a gear and a "…"

Rejected: a third icon button on the right of the header beside the print split button and the pane toggle, for two short menus.

## Decisions for Kenneth

1. Kebab or gear: Option A with "…", or Option B with a gear on both screens.
2. Keep Recent projects in the menu, or send people to Home for it.
3. Whether to add Keyboard shortcuts and Report a problem now, and the destination for the latter.
4. The Tab leak to OrcaSlicer's Preview: block it in the shell, or keep a conditional Back row.

## Side finding, outside the menu

The project name and save state are not continuously visible on Prepare when the pane is closed; today they live in the "…" button's tooltip and in the Project tab. That is a product-definition gap on its own, whichever menu option is chosen.
EOF

name: jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact
description: "The two Claude artifacts mirroring the Figma file JusPrin v2 (a Design System and a Design canvas): URLs, where the re-sync tools and backups live, how a re-sync is proven safe, what was measured on 2026-10-13, known gaps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 18e047ce-4892-4a44-8b70-c447eb34727c
  modified: 2026-10-13T20:50:06.847Z
---

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.

Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=<tmp>` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then.

**Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts`
were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added
directly in the artifact). Running build_components.py or assembling from those sources regresses the live
bundle. Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools
sources from the patched result; `tools/composer/add_turn_line_boards.py` and the ChatTurnActivity card
were done that way. The DS page generates `tokens.css` itself: never publish it to the DS, only to the
canvas's `project/ds/jusprin/` copy. Adding a coded component = patch bundle.js (function + header list +
__EXPORTS__), bundle.css, index.d.ts (props + window typing), tokens.json, a hand-written
`components/<Name>/preview.html` card with `@dsCard height=` measured by rendering it with React from unpkg,
README.md's component list, and `design-system.json` lastChange in the last call.

**2026-10-26 (setup card rework):** `tools/composer/setup_card_lib.py` draws the two-part card as board markup, spec lines and the coded component from one props dict; `build_setup_card_rework.py` runs the whole rework (cards, screens, calibration, sticky, new, canvas, ds) into `work-setup-card/`. The mirror's `published/canvas` had drifted by three onboarding-v1 boards (fetched back); the live canvas.json, not the mirror's, is the base for an index publish. Version ids before and after each publish are logged in the README ("Versions before the setup-card rework"): the tool cannot list versions, so write them down at publish time. Both artifacts' versions bump when their Artifact type re-releases, so a new version id alone does not mean content changed. `tools/bundle.src.*` and `index.src.d.ts` were refreshed from the published bundle; `heights.json` in the work dir holds every measured board height.
=====CANVAS-RULES=====
---
name: canvas-boards-from-bundle-rules
description: "Kenneth's 2026-10-21 correction: a canvas board I draw must copy the Design System bundle's CSS rules and the app's own markup, never an older board or memory; the calibration page had 14 px menu rows drawn at 13, a missing Connect… row, a black Remove, a stale reply-choice style and more."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 9ce2f3c8-7b6d-4ba7-99ce-889f9d9f192a
  modified: 2026-10-22T00:09:35.890Z
---

Kenneth, 2026-10-21, on the calibration page I drew: "It looks like you didn't follow this hygiene. read design
guidelines in readme, and fix your own sloppiness", then "I suspect there were more sloppiness in the boards you
designed". He was right on both counts. I had copied markup from older canvas boards (the printer-menu board at
13 px rows, the stale ds-chat-reply-choice board) and from memory (a Home kebab with no Connect…, a black Remove,
a 220 px width, the filament menu in an old order), instead of from the two sources that are authoritative.

**Why:** rule 5 of "Writing UI code" (agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md) says the design system wins, and the
design system's truth is its coded bundle (`figma-mirror/published/ds/project/components/bundle.css`, classes
`.jp-*`), not any one board on the canvas: boards drift (the printer-menu board draws rows at 13 px, the reply
choice board draws the pre-capsule style). For surfaces the bundle has no component for (the printer receipt, a
sent photo in a message), the app's own CSS and TSX are the source.

**How to apply:** before drawing a board, dump the bundle rules for every component used (`grep '\.jp-<name>'
bundle.css`) and read the app's row set for every menu (Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp, Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp,
HomeUI PrinterMenu.tsx) and the app's CSS for chat pieces (AgentUI/styles.css). Also wrong the first time: the chat header named the project where the app names the chat (3 to 7 words, kConversationTitleInstructions); the pinned card was the stale "CURRENT SETUP · See all" board, not the app's Setup summary (`.current-setup*`: label + state header in Metadata Bold, purpose as Body Bold title, presets line, plan headline, Label Bold metrics with 14 px glyphs, hairline, All settings link; out of date drops the accent and uses the attention block); the composer placeholder was not the approved board's. Draw rows at Body 14 / 36 px
(`.jp-menu-row`), popovers on surface-raised 280 wide, reply choices as capsules on surface-subtle, user
bubbles 10/12 padding radius-medium at 75% width, tool cards on surface-subtle, project cards 293 wide with
one status line, and no annotation tags ("NEW") inside a drawn component. State in the caption which rows are
new. Known DS-vs-canvas inconsistency not mine to settle: `.jp-bubble-agent` has an avatar; the app and the
timeline boards draw agent prose without one. Related: [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]],
[[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[calibration-design-decisions]].
=====WATCH=====

name: artifact-watch-crosstalk
description: "Publishing a design artifact arms a comment watch with auto-replies in that session; when several sessions work on the same artifact, each one answers the others' comments. Stop the watch after publishing unless Kenneth wants that session to handle comments."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 184d4aaf-cfcf-432d-ac3c-191a0b1f6a05
  modified: 2026-10-21T12:37:33.441Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth found another session's canvas comments (a "Calibration · Printer & Filament" page) being auto-replied to and reported in this session, and asked how to make this session ignore it.

Cause: every publish to a Claude artifact arms a watch with comment auto-replies in the publishing session. Two sessions working on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v) or the Design System (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) both get every comment sent to Claude, wherever it is on the artifact.

**Why:** the wrong session answers a thread about work it doesn't know, and its reply can contradict the session that owns the boards.

**How to apply:** after a publish, stop the watch (ArtifactComments action "watch", on: false) unless Kenneth said this session owns the artifact's comments. Re-read the live artifact before publishing again, since another session may have published since. Related: [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]], [[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]].
=====SOURCE=====
---
name: design-source-is-claude-artifacts
description: "2026-10-20: Figma is retired for JusPrin design; the Claude Design System and JusPrin v2 canvas artifacts are the source of truth. Don't propose Figma changes or cite Figma."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 1ad40aa6-b204-449c-8be8-7600964a4f52
  modified: 2026-10-27T20:28:20.888Z
---

Kenneth, 2026-10-20: "We're not changing Figma anymore. We have migrated to
Cloud artifact." The two Claude artifacts are now the design source of truth:
the Design System (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the
"JusPrin v2" canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v). They
started as copies of Figma ([[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]]), but
they are no longer re-synced from it.

**Why:** design changes now happen in the artifacts, so a Figma-based argument
or a "change Figma" proposal points at a dead file.

**How to apply:** check designs by reading the artifact files (Artifact read
with `path`, e.g. `project/<page>-<frame>.dc.html` on the canvas); never
suggest editing Figma or waiting for Figma seat allowance; when citing a
design, name the artifact board, not a Figma node. Describe what the board
actually draws, not what a component's internal properties imply: a menu row
with no fill or border draws no shape at all, so it is not "a square row".
Older memories that say "Figma is the source of truth"
([[design-token-sync-decisions]], [[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]) are superseded on
that point.

**Restated by Kenneth later on 2026-10-20:** "from now on, we should assume claude design artifact is the up to date design. figma is out of date." Docs changed the same day (uncommitted on jusprin-newui): agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md no longer points at Figma, and the repo skill .claude/skills/figma-agent-design is marked retired.

**Also frozen (Kenneth, 2026-10-27):** the old Claude Design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts" (claude.ai/design/p/d981c5e2-…, files like `Orca Chat Panel.dc.html`). It is history for how a decision was reached, never the current design. For the chat panel, including G-code entries and print bands, the current boards are the five `main-print-timeline-panel-full*` boards on the canvas's Main Page. **The canvas moved (2026-10-27):** VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v is itself frozen ("JusPrin v2 (frozen 2026-10-27)" title, a `frozen-pointer-*` note on every page). The current canvas is https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, with numbered board names (`main-05-print-timeline-panel-full-no-revert`, `main-07-…full`, `agent-ui-01-timeline-cards-manufacturing-history-state-matrix`) and shared parts as `<dc-import>` components that render.py can't draw. Check the canvas title before editing. On it (version 1793132250-e29e) `plates-26e3-project-print-history` and the state matrix were redrawn to the G-code design (matrix now 3 variants, 772 px tall). I also edited 26e3 on the frozen canvas by mistake (version 1793132033-a81d); at Kenneth's request it was restored byte-for-byte to the original BUILD 1 board in version 1793132895-0706.

**How to apply:** when a memory note, commit message, doc or old plan cites a Figma frame, node id or value, treat it as history and check the artifact board instead. Edit the artifacts directly (recipe in [[jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact]]); never re-sync them from Figma, which would overwrite newer design.

description: "The two Claude artifacts mirroring the Figma file JusPrin v2 (a Design System and a Design canvas): URLs, where the re-sync tools and backups live, how a re-sync is proven safe, what was measured on 2026-10-13, known gaps."

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.

Publishing (2026-10-20, filament step): a publish is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version" unless this session did a plain `read` of the artifact url (path reads alone do not count). Headless Chrome hangs when another Chrome holds the default profile: pass `--user-data-dir=<tmp>` (render.py now does). MenuRow has `detail`, `detailTone: 'warning'` and `meta` since then.

**Trap found 2026-10-20 (turn line work):** `figma-mirror/tools/bundle.src.js`, `bundle.src.css` and `index.src.d.ts`
were STALE against the live Design System bundle (menu-row detail/meta and the Composer menus had been added
directly in the artifact). Running build_components.py or assembling from those sources regresses the live
bundle. Patch the live files (published/… copies, verified equal to the artifact by sha) and refresh the tools
sources from the patched result; `tools/composer/add_turn_line_boards.py` and the ChatTurnActivity card
were done that way. The DS page generates `tokens.css` itself: never publish it to the DS, only to the
canvas's `project/ds/jusprin/` copy. Adding a coded component = patch bundle.js (function + header list +
__EXPORTS__), bundle.css, index.d.ts (props + window typing), tokens.json, a hand-written
`components/<Name>/preview.html` card with `@dsCard height=` measured by rendering it with React from unpkg,
README.md's component list, and `design-system.json` lastChange in the last call.

**2026-10-26 (setup card rework):** `tools/composer/setup_card_lib.py` draws the two-part card as board markup, spec lines and the coded component from one props dict; `build_setup_card_rework.py` runs the whole rework (cards, screens, calibration, sticky, new, canvas, ds) into `work-setup-card/`. The mirror's `published/canvas` had drifted by three onboarding-v1 boards (fetched back); the live canvas.json, not the mirror's, is the base for an index publish. Version ids before and after each publish are logged in the README ("Versions before the setup-card rework"): the tool cannot list versions, so write them down at publish time. Both artifacts' versions bump when their Artifact type re-releases, so a new version id alone does not mean content changed. `tools/bundle.src.*` and `index.src.d.ts` were refreshed from the published bundle; `heights.json` in the work dir holds every measured board height.

# Figma mirror: tools and backups

> **2026-10-20: Figma is retired and out of date.** The two Claude artifacts are now the up-to-date JusPrin
> design. Do NOT re-sync them from Figma: that would overwrite newer design work. Edit them directly:
> copy the live files into `work/` (or read them with the Artifact tool), change them, publish only the changed
> files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. Remember the canvas keeps its own copy of the design system in
> `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens and component styles): change both artifacts together. `tools/composer/` holds
> the scripts used since then (`render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome; `resize_board.py` fixes a
> board's height in its file and in `canvas.json`; `build_filament_step.py` draws the Add-a-printer step-3 boards and their spec files, `measure_sheets.py` measures their sheet heights with headless Chrome). Before publishing to either artifact, do a plain `read` of its url: a publish after only `path` reads is refused as "haven't viewed the latest version". The Figma re-sync steps below are kept as history.


This folder keeps what is needed to re-sync two Claude artifacts with the Figma file "JusPrin v2"
(file key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`), and to prove a re-sync breaks nothing.

- Canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
- JusPrin Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL

It lives outside the JusPrin repo on purpose: it is not product code, and untracked files in the repo mean
"unfinished work" there.

## What is here

- `published/` — an exact copy of what is published now (`canvas/project`, `ds/project`). Every re-sync is
  compared against it, then it is replaced by the new build.
- `figma/spec3/<page id>.txt` — the Figma pages as last read (one text line per layer). `figma/vars.json` —
  Figma's variables, text styles and shadows as last read.
- `tools/` — the scripts (below).
- `visual/figma/*.png` — Figma's own screenshot of each page, used to score the artboards.
  `visual/scores-*.json` — the scores before and after the 2026-10-13 re-import.
- `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` — the published files, the Figma reads and the scripts as they were
